core_obligations: Record that one implication is immediate, and assume the second formulation with some presentation (proof lines 4697).

For a representable etale affine formal algebraic space over the given space, form the fibre products with the members of the presentation, choose coverings of them, and use quasi-compactness to select finitely many members whose coproduct covers the given object (proof lines 4699-4712).

Transfer the type to each selected member using the statement on affine morphisms over an affine formal algebraic space, and to their finite coproduct -- a step the author marks as omitted -- using that finite disjoint unions of affine formal algebraic spaces are affine and have the type (proof lines 4712-4718).
Conclude by the two-way statement for each of the five types (proof lines 4718-4729).
proof_roadmap: Finite refinement of a covering by quasi-compactness (proof lines 4699-4712).
Transfer of the type to the members and their coproduct (proof lines 4712-4718).
Conclusion by the five two-way statements (proof lines 4718-4729).
difficulty_reason: For a formal algebraic space and one of the five types -- countably indexed, countably indexed and classical, weakly adic, adic*, Noetherian -- the lemma asserts the equivalence of two formulations: that every representable etale affine formal algebraic space over it has the type, and that the members of some presentation have the type (statement lines 4681-4695). One implication is immediate; the substance is the other. Given a representable etale affine formal algebraic space over the space and a presentation, the fibre products of the given object with the members of the presentation are formal algebraic spaces, so coverings of them may be chosen, and quasi-compactness of the given object allows finitely many members of these coverings to be selected so that their coproduct covers it and is etale over it (proof lines 4697-4712). Each selected member inherits the type from the corresponding member of the presentation by the statement on affine morphisms over an affine formal algebraic space, and the finite coproduct of them does too -- a step the author marks as a small detail omitted concerning finite disjoint unions (proof lines 4712-4718). The conclusion then follows from the corresponding two-way statement for each of the five types (proof lines 4718-4729). The claim is H2: the argument combines a finite refinement by quasi-compactness with two transfers of the type, and it collects the five cases into one statement by citing the five corresponding equivalence results.
